summary:
Giving coordinates or an objecs name, dates and bands of light. Taking data from multiple sources (NASA/CSA/your data), in this project you will be able to compare different sources on the same objects. You can compare brightness through time, position through time and the infrared spectrum graph. You can do short processing on the images to get the best data you can.

You can also compare your new data with previus data, like in aladin sky atlas, which has data all the way back to 1997. So drastic movements can be compared easily and fast.
details:
EpochX is a web tool that shows SPHEREx sky images as a video. You enter a name or coordinates and watch the same patch of sky change over time, so moving objects stand out. It places Canadian CADC data next to SPHEREx, measures the object’s position, brightness and infrared spectrum, and warns when a result may not be real motion. Users can also upload their own telescope images and compare them with SPHEREx and the Canadian data.

EpochX aims to make SPHEREx data easy for anyone to explore, including the public, students and amateur astronomers. Users can see how the sky changes and spot moving objects such as brown dwarfs and fast-moving stars, without handling raw data. It also lets people combine their own telescope images with space-mission data, so they can contribute to real observations.

Tools: SPHEREx (IRSA), CADC, Gaia, SIMBAD, Aladin, astrometry.net, Claude.

Languages: Python (astropy), JS, HTML, CSS
